system.description: The power causes a tree to uproot and collapse. The power is laid in the ground directly beneath a tree and there forms a small uproot. As soon as the power has been woven, the power begins to swell up like a bloated cow’s stomach. Soon the power expands so much that the tree above it is wrenched from the soil and tipped over. An observer can see that something is happening because the soil suddenly starts to shift and rise. In the fourth action round of the power, the uproot grows so large that it bursts out of the ground, and in the fifth action round it finally tips the tree over and then disappears. For a tree to be toppled in this manner, it cannot have a trunk with a circumference larger than 1.5 meters at ground level. If the trunk is larger, the power will not have enough strength to tip it over. The mopor, who must c oncentrate on the uprooting at all times, can choose which way the tree will fall. If she loses concentration or loses control over the uproot for any reason, it will still continue to swell until the tree falls, but the game master will determine the direction. Everyone who observes this occurrence and was unaware of the mopor’s actions must immediately make a Situation roll with a Situation value of 6 (Psyche modifiers apply) to avoid receiving 1d10 Fear Points when the uproot breaks out of the ground. On a success, an observer receives no Fear Points. The uproot could just as easily be placed under a large rock, open ground, or even a house. The final results of such an action and how much of the object collapses or is tipped over is up to the game master to decide. The uproot in the power’s basic version can lift or tip approximately 100 kg.
system.summary: Makes a tree grow and uproot itself to create an obstacle or crush what lies in its fall.
